name: Maps
description: A map of every place your room has: the places you have saved and the items other modules put somewhere. Pick a spot to save a new place.
author: Coffee Pub

permissions.label: See the map and its places
Save places from the map and put items on it

settings.label: Map source
settings.help: Where the map itself comes from.

options.label: A map file on this server
options.help: Tavern reads a PMTiles map file that you put in the map-tiles folder of this module's folder on the server. Nothing is sent to anyone else: the map works offline and nobody outside sees where your places are. A city is a few megabytes, a country hundreds, the world well over 100 GB.

options.label: A map file at a web address
options.help:
Tavern reads a PMTiles map file from the address you give below, so the map does not have to be stored on this server.
Every person's browser contacts that host directly. The host can see their internet address and roughly which area they are looking at. Choose a host you trust, and tell the people who use this server.
The host must allow requests from this server's pages (CORS) and support range requests, as static hosting and most content delivery networks do. Its terms, cost and reliability are yours to check. Only https addresses work.
The credit © OpenStreetMap contributors always stays on the map.

settings.label: Map files
settings.help: PMTiles map files in modules/maps/map-tiles/ in the data folder. Tick the ones to use; several regions are drawn together.

settings.label: Map file address
settings.help: An https link to a .pmtiles file, for example https://maps.example.org/region.pmtiles

settings.label: World file, for cutting a region
settings.help: A world PMTiles file to cut a region from with "Add a region", below. Tavern reads only the part it cuts, over https range requests, never the whole file. Protomaps publishes a daily build at https://maps.protomaps.com/builds; its address is dated and changes most days (for example https://build.protomaps.com/20260921.pmtiles), so check that page for today's, or point this at your own stable copy. Left empty, cutting a region is off.
